openFindings.title: A path deleted before dispatch is subtracted from detection forever
openFindings.evidence: detectNewOutOfScopeViolations skips any baseline path whose recorded hash is empty; a deleted-at-baseline path hashes to '' because git hash-object exits non-zero on a missing file (write-containment.ts:787, 425-429).
openFindings.recommendation: Track a distinct baseline state for unhashable-but-recorded paths (deleted/absent) and re-evaluate them with the content-identity check when they reappear, instead of treating an empty hash as unmatched.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the full detection path and baseline snapshot function; grepped the unit suite for a deleted-at-baseline case and found none (write-containment.vitest.ts covers leaf-deletes and leaf-modifies only).

openFindings.title: The churn detector's first window is never counted
openFindings.evidence: The sampler's first sample sets previousPaths and contributes newlyDirty=0; the sampler is only fed by the progress heartbeat, which first fires one cadence after dispatch (fanout-run.cjs:3272-3283). Writes landing before that sample are absorbed as the baseline.
openFindings.recommendation: Seed the detector's first sample from the pre-dispatch baseline snapshot (already captured at fanout-run.cjs:3223-3231) so the first heartbeat window is measured rather than assumed quiet.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the detector factory, its call sites, and the heartbeat wiring; confirmed the first sample cannot fire before the first heartbeat by reading startLineageProgressHeartbeat's interval setup.

openFindings.title: NFR-P01's single-invocation claim undercounts the churn sampler
openFindings.evidence: Each sample calls snapshotOutOfScopeDirtyPaths, which runs two rev-parse calls (write-containment.ts:385-393 via resolveArtifactScope:616-621), one status --porcelain, and one hash-object per dirty path (write-containment.ts:787). NFR-P01 (spec.md:183) promises one status invocation per heartbeat.
openFindings.recommendation: Either narrow the sampler to a status-only read (skip hashing when only paths are needed) or amend NFR-P01 to state the real per-heartbeat cost.
openFindings.scopeProof: Traced the sampler's call chain to the git helpers and counted every spawnSync that executes per sample; no caching exists between samples.

openFindings.title: The containment repo root can resolve to a subdirectory while all guard paths are repo-relative
openFindings.evidence: resolveContainmentRepoRoot returns cwd unless the artifact tree lives in a different worktree, while resolveArtifactScope derives artifactRelPosix from repoRoot and compares it against porcelain paths, which git emits relative to the worktree root regardless of -C (verified with git -C specs/system-deep-loop status --porcelain).
openFindings.recommendation: Resolve the guard root to the git toplevel (the helper already has gitToplevel) or assert that cwd is the toplevel before containment runs.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the resolver, its only caller (fanout-run.cjs:2813-2817), and the containment scope math; verified git's porcelain path basis with a live read-only git invocation from a subdirectory.

openFindings.title: Baseline-targeted restore follows a symlink and can write outside the working tree
openFindings.evidence: writeFileSync(join(repoRoot, violation.path), baselineBytes) opens with w and follows a final-component symlink; the HEAD branch uses git checkout and does not.
openFindings.recommendation: Refuse to restore a path that is not a regular file (lstat) or open with O_NOFOLLOW; fall back to preserving the path and reporting it.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the full revert function, the baseline reader and the HEAD branch; grepped for lstat/O_NOFOLLOW/realpath guards before the write and found none.

openFindings.title: The quarantine writer does not canonicalize its destination
openFindings.evidence: NFR-S01 promises the quarantine writer never follows a symlink out of the directory; writeQuarantineFile mkdirs and writes along a string-joined destination path with no canonicalization.
openFindings.recommendation: Canonicalize the destination root once and assert each write stays inside it before writing.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the quarantine writer, its destination construction and the detector's canonicalization rule for comparison.

openFindings.title: Quarantine copies out-of-scope file content into a publishable artifact plane
openFindings.evidence: Baseline capture copies every dirty out-of-scope file into the lineage directory (write-containment.ts:790-798) and quarantine copies violated paths again; the packet's own summary records 893 files at 8.2 MB captured from eight other packets' work.
openFindings.recommendation: Document the exposure and consider an operator-facing opt-out for baseline content capture on a dirty shared checkout.
openFindings.scopeProof: Traced the capture calls, read the size bounds, and cross-checked the packet's recorded live-run measurement.

openFindings.title: The removed containment.worktrees key is silently accepted
openFindings.evidence: The schema dropped worktrees with no z.never() guard, while the same block guards the removed stopPolicy key for exactly the silent-drop reason.
openFindings.recommendation: Add a z.never().optional() guard for worktrees, matching the stopPolicy precedent.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the containment schema, its comment block and the packet docs that documented the key.

openFindings.title: The spec still mandates the worktree mechanism the packet removed while reading Complete
openFindings.evidence: REQ-005 (:133), REQ-007 (:141) and REQ-008 (:142), SC-003 (:155), SC-005 (:157), NFR-R02 (:200) and the frontmatter (description :3, trigger phrases :8, executive summary :22, key decisions :24, critical dependencies :26) all mandate per-lineage worktrees; the phase map on the same page records 007-worktree-removal complete (:116) and ca713e3478 deleted the five worktree modules and their suites.
openFindings.recommendation: Mark REQ-005/007/008, SC-003/005 and NFR-R02 Superseded by ADR-007 and rewrite the frontmatter, executive summary, key decisions and dependencies to the shipped shared-checkout design.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read every requirement row, success criterion and frontmatter claim against the phase map, ADR-007, the deletion commit and the current runtime tree.

openFindings.title: The acceptance criteria remain In Progress and their Met evidence cites deleted files and out-of-range lines
openFindings.evidence: File unchanged in the reviewed range; Status In Progress (:50) dated 2026-09-13 (:14) against spec Complete; AC-015 cites deleted worktree-lifecycle.vitest.ts:531/:547; AC-009/012/013/014/017/018 cite fanout-run.vitest.ts lines 4309/4400/4456/4504/4547/4181/4260/4395/3130/4184/4212/4228 beyond the file's 4374 lines; :107 claims every criterion Met including the worktree default.
openFindings.recommendation: Mark AC-009 and AC-012..AC-018 Superseded by ADR-007 in the waiver cells, re-anchor the remaining citations, and re-date the metadata against HEAD.
openFindings.scopeProof: Diffed the file against the reviewed range (no commits touch it); resolved every cited path and line number against HEAD.

openFindings.title: implementation-summary.md states the reversal in one paragraph and presents the mechanism as shipped everywhere else
openFindings.evidence: Line 61 states the removal, but the frontmatter (:3), files table (:67), verification narrative (:75), key decisions (:87-88), five verification rows (:103-109) and known limitations 5-10 and 19 (:124-129, :140) still describe live worktrees with the removed suite sizes.
openFindings.recommendation: Strike or mark superseded every worktree row and limitation, and keep one paragraph recording the reversal.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the summary end to end and cross-checked each worktree claim against HEAD.

openFindings.title: tasks.md still records the removed worktree phase as delivered with deleted-suite evidence
openFindings.evidence: T017-T022, T028, T030-T033 are checked with evidence naming the deleted worktree-lifecycle and worktree-lease suites (:87-103, :124); CHK-002/003/023/100/112/113/121/124/130/151 assert worktree behaviour (:168-169, :191, :256, :269-270, :279, :282, :290, :316); the file holds 91 checked boxes and zero unchecked.

openFindings.scopeProof: Read the phase-4 block and every CHK row mentioning worktrees; counted checked/unchecked boxes.

openFindings.title: handover.md briefs a cold session on the removed worktree default
openFindings.evidence: Line 37 states per-lineage worktrees are off by default with --worktrees true; the worktree cost figures remain (:41-42); the cold-read order sends readers to ADR-004 for the worktree-default decision (:100) without naming ADR-007.
openFindings.recommendation: Rewrite the cold-start brief around the single shared-checkout path and ADR-007.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the handoff's status, costs and cold-read sections against ADR-006/007 and the current runtime.

openFindings.title: goal.md's durable slice still records the worktree default flip as the live decision
openFindings.evidence: Continuity recent_action names the worktree default flip (:16); the answered question records ADR-004 turning the default on (:32); D5/D6 describe the ephemeral worktree and --worktrees true (:61-62); the Implementation row lists per-lineage worktrees as done (:114, :124); D7 (:63) records the removal, so adjacent rows contradict.
openFindings.recommendation: Amend the continuity fields and the D5/D6 rows to the shipped design, keeping D7 as the superseding entry.
openFindings.scopeProof: Compared the durable slice's decisions and status rows with ADR-006/007 and the shipped schema.

openFindings.title: The spec's own section-7 justification contradicts REQ-004's shipped thresholds
openFindings.evidence: REQ-004 (:139) states the shipped defaults as three newly dirty paths per window or twelve cumulative, while the section-7 prose REQ-004 cites still says twelve per window and forty cumulative (:192).
openFindings.recommendation: Update the rationale prose to the shipped numbers, or state explicitly that the rationale was written for the original draft.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read REQ-004 and the section it cites; cross-checked against executor-config.ts defaults (3/12).

openFindings.title: REQ-006's both-loop-protocols clause is half migrated and two stale comment blocks contradict the sweep claim
openFindings.evidence: deep-research's loop-protocol.md:287-290 carries the full containment ruleset while deep-review's contains none (only the cli-opencode sandbox note at :280); hub SKILL.md:128 points readers at the research file; the superseded 'revert ... fail-closed' comments remain above the advisory calls at deep-review-auto.yaml:1517-1519 and deep-research-auto.yaml:1621-1623; AC-011 records a zero-occurrence sweep.
openFindings.recommendation: Mirror the ruleset into deep-review's protocol, correct the two comment blocks, and re-run the sweep with the result recorded.
openFindings.scopeProof: Grepped both loop protocols for containment rules, read the hub bullet, and read both comment blocks above the migrated calls.

openFindings.title: The cli-opencode dispatch guard still requires an isolated linked worktree and now always throws
openFindings.evidence: The if_cli_opencode branch throws when rev-parse --git-dir equals --git-common-dir (:1308-1310), requires the primary main/master worktree clean (:1321) and all changes inside the artifact dir (:1362), and logs recovery_baseline with worktree: repoRoot (:1368); no command asset creates a worktree any more and the YAML was untouched in the reviewed range, so an inline cli-opencode dispatch in the shared checkout always fails before dispatch.
openFindings.recommendation: Remove the linked-worktree precondition (keep the artifact-dir and prompt-section checks) or replace it with a deliberate, documented refusal; sweep the command assets again as part of the removal.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the whole guard branch, searched all four command YAMLs for worktree creation, and confirmed no commit in the reviewed range edits the file.

openFindings.title: NFR-R01 claims a fail-open property the module does not implement
openFindings.evidence: NFR-R01 promises containment returns empty when the artifact directory is outside the worktree; write-containment.ts throws when resolveArtifactScope returns null while a git toplevel resolves; CHK-013 in tasks.md:180 records the same claim as verified.
openFindings.recommendation: Either amend NFR-R01 to the real behaviour or make the artifact-outside-worktree case fail open as stated.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the guard's scope resolution and the non-functional table; confirmed the throw path and that shipped callers never reach it.

openFindings.title: Ten byte-identical inline containment call blocks duplicate the same options and message across four command YAMLs
openFindings.evidence: The same six-option call and advisory message are copied at deep-research-auto.yaml:1244/1334/1424/1625, deep-research-confirm.yaml:1119, deep-review-auto.yaml:1521/1615/1705/1795 and deep-review-confirm.yaml:1191; two copies already carry stale comments and none can pass the mode option.
openFindings.recommendation: Extract one shared helper that performs the call, prints the advisory and returns the result, leaving each dispatch branch a one-line invocation.
openFindings.scopeProof: Printed all ten call blocks and compared them; verified the runtime guard is the single tested implementation while the call-site envelope has no test.

openFindings.title: The index-lock contention warning is drained only by the fan-out runner
openFindings.evidence: drainGitContentionWarnings is exported at write-containment.ts:312 and called only at fanout-run.cjs:3171; the ten inline callers never drain, so an exhausted retry budget in an inline iteration is recorded and silently discarded.
openFindings.recommendation: Drain and log inside the shared helper, or log at record time inside the guard.
openFindings.scopeProof: Grepped every caller of drainGitContentionWarnings across the runtime; one drain site exists.

openFindings.title: The decision record's supersession chain leaves two removed-mechanism ADRs looking live
openFindings.evidence: ADR-003 (detached ephemeral lane) remains Status Proposed at :234-240 though implemented in phase 4 and deleted in phase 7; ADR-005 (checkout watch for isolated lanes) remains Status Accepted at :466-472 though no isolated lanes exist; ADR-007 :540-542 names only ADR-004 and ADR-006.
openFindings.recommendation: Mark ADR-003 Withdrawn/Superseded and ADR-005 Superseded by ADR-007; extend ADR-007's note to cover both.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read every ADR status and the supersession notes in ADR-006 and ADR-007; cross-checked the removed code paths.

openFindings.title: The artifact-scope containment rule is implemented twice with no shared helper
openFindings.evidence: The cli-opencode guard defines canonicalLocation/escapesArtifactDir (:1328-1360) implementing the same name-plus-canonical rule as isContainedInArtifact in write-containment.ts:574-596, but the module's helper is not exported so the YAML reimplements it with a copied rationale comment.
openFindings.recommendation: Export the canonicalization helper from the module and call it from the command guard.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read both implementations and the module's export list; confirmed the helper is internal and the guard cannot import it.

openFindings.title: The runtime fan-out catalog entry is stale and names its third CLI kind twice
openFindings.evidence: The entry lists '(opencode, claude, opencode)' at :3 and 'cli-opencode, cli-claude-code, cli-opencode' at :42 while the code maps cli-codex as the third kind (fanout-run.cjs:473-475); its HOW-IT-WORKS section (:40-59) predates containment enforcement, the churn sampler, the advisory status and the index-lock retry; the file was untouched in the reviewed range while the hub catalog entry was migrated by ca713e3478.
openFindings.recommendation: Correct the kind list and add the driver's post-045 responsibilities, or point related references at the hub containment entry explicitly.
openFindings.scopeProof: Compared the entry's claims against the kind map and the post-045 runner behavior; checked the file's history in the reviewed range.

openFindings.title: The empty-registry advisory tests the research key and misfires on every review lane
openFindings.evidence: hasLineageKeyFindings accepts only registry.keyFindings (:868), the research reducer's key (deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:2353), while the review reducer writes openFindings (runtime/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:1557) and the review registry list is exactly ['deep-review-findings-registry.json'] (:825-828); the only test uses a research lane with no registry (fanout-run.vitest.ts:4303-4373).
openFindings.recommendation: Accept openFindings (and the coerced findings alias) for review, or delegate emptiness detection to the merge's registry normalization so both agree.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the check, the review and research registries and their reducers, the registry file lists, and the only covering test.
